q: 1. Drawing is the Engineers'
explain: A drawing conveys shape, size and construction information graphically, so it is called the universal language of engineers.

q: 2. Maximum distance between black board and last row of benches should not be more than ...... in school buildings.
explain: School building design norms specify a maximum blackboard-to-last-bench distance of 7 m to ensure visibility for all students.

q: 3. The geometrical name of the curvature of the coil used in spiral binding is
explain: The spiral binding coil does not correspond to any of the standard mathematical spiral curves (Archimedean, logarithmic) or an involute; hence the answer is 'none of these'.

q: 4. Which of the following methods is not used for drawing elliptical curves?
explain: Ellipses are commonly constructed by the intersecting-arcs, concentric-circles, or oblong (rectangle) methods; there is no standard 'tangent method' for drawing an ellipse.

q: 5. A building drawing consists of
explain: A complete building drawing set includes the site plan, floor plans, elevations, sections, and foundation details, so 'all of these' is correct.

q: 6. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: A sectional view is created by imagining the object cut by a plane to reveal and clarify hidden internal features that are not visible in a normal view.

q: 7. In case of aligned method of dimensioning, they can be readable form .............
options: bottoms and right side of drawing sheet
bottoms and left side of drawing sheet
bottoms and top side of drawing sheet
explain: In the aligned system, dimensions are placed so they can be read from the bottom edge and the right-hand edge of the drawing sheet.

q: 8. To facilitate extension, entries in the table should begin form .............
explain: Tables designed for future additions are conventionally filled starting from the bottom row upward, leaving room to extend entries above as needed.

q: 9. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off .............
explain: A full section is obtained by passing a cutting plane completely through the object, conceptually removing (cutting away) one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 10. Dashed (dotted) line is used for indication
explain: Dashed lines represent features that are not visible from the current point of view but exist within or behind the object.

q: 11. The lines which are drawn to represent visible edges and surface boundaries of objects are called ............
explain: Visible edges are represented by continuous thick lines known as object lines, outlines, or principal lines.

q: 12. The unseen/inner edge of an object is represented by
explain: Similar to hidden lines, these are represented by short dashes (often referred to as 'dotted' in older textbooks).

q: 13. In case of unidirectional method of dimensioning, they can be read form .............
options: bottom side of drawing sheet only
right side of drawing sheet only
top side of drawing sheet only
left side of drawing sheet only
explain: In the unidirectional dimensioning system, all dimension figures are written horizontally so that they can be read from the bottom of the drawing sheet only, regardless of the direction of the dimension line.

q: 14. Dimension lines and projection line in the drawing are shown by .............
explain: As per drawing conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines, distinguishing them from thick outlines and dashed hidden lines.

q: 15. System of placing dimension on a drawing work is .............
explain: Dimensions can be placed using either the aligned system (figures aligned with the dimension line) or the unidirectional system (figures always read from the bottom); both are recognized methods.

q: 16. In case of unidirectional method of dimensioning, they can be read from
options: bottom side of drawing sheet only
right side of drawing sheet only
top side of drawing sheet only
left side of drawing sheet only
explain: Unidirectional dimensioning keeps all text horizontal, regardless of the line's direction, so they are always read from the bottom.

q: 17. System of placing dimension on a drawing work is
explain: Dimensions may be placed using either the aligned method or the unidirectional method, so both systems are valid.

q: 18. The main purpose of leader line is
options: to connect a note with the feature
explain: Leader lines are thin lines used to point to a specific part of a drawing to provide descriptions or dimensions.

q: 19. Hatching line is a line which makes an angle of 45 degree with
explain: Hatching (section lines) should be drawn at $45^{\circ}$ relative to the main boundaries or center lines of the object.

q: 20. Art of writing title, notes etc. on a drawing is called .............
explain: The skill/art of writing titles, notes, and dimensions on engineering drawings in a standardized, legible style is called lettering.

q: 21. The main purpose of leader line is in the drawing is .............
options: to connect a note with the feature
explain: Note: per the given answer key, this item's marked answer is 'to show hatch'; however conventionally a leader line is used to connect a note/dimension to the specific feature it refers to on the drawing.

q: 22. The dimension system is unidirectional if
options: dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom and right hand edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from anywhere of the drawing sheet
explain: In the unidirectional dimensioning system all figures are written horizontally so the whole drawing can be read from the bottom edge of the sheet only.

q: 23. Size of letter means the ............. of the letter.
explain: In lettering standards, the 'size' of a letter refers to its height, which determines the overall scale/legibility of the lettering on a drawing.

q: 24. Symbol .......indicates
explain: Irregular interlocking shapes represent stone masonry, whereas parallel diagonal lines usually represent brick.

q: 25. The set of technical drawings used during the manufacturing phase of a product. including civil construction, are known as:
explain: Drawings that guide the actual manufacturing/construction process are called working drawings.

q: 26. Working drawing is prepared not for .............
explain: Working drawings are used to prepare bills of quantities, cost estimation, and construction layout on site, but they themselves are drawings, not written specifications (specifications are a separate document).

q: 27. When a pyramid or cone is cut by a cutting plane parallel to its base, the remaining portion thus obtained after removing the top portion is called ...
explain: A frustum is the base part of a cone or pyramid that remains after the top is sliced off by a plane parallel to the base.

q: 28. The locus of a point lying on the circumference of the circle which rolls on a straight line is known as .............
explain: A cycloid is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on the circumference of a circle as it rolls without slipping along a straight line.

q: 29. The dimension system is unidirectional if .............
options: dimension in the drawing sheet be red from bottom edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from bottom and right hand edge of the drawing sheet
dimension in the drawing sheet be read from anywhere of the drawing sheet
explain: Note: per the answer key, option (b) is marked correct; the unidirectional system's defining rule is that all dimension figures are oriented horizontally so they are read only from the bottom edge of the sheet.

q: 30. The included angle of a pentagon is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, option (b) 72° is marked correct; this corresponds to the central (apex) angle of a regular pentagon when divided into 5 equal triangles from its center (360°/5 = 72°), while the interior angle of a pentagon is actually 108°.

q: 31. The locus of a point is a ......... when it moves in a plane in such a way that its distance from a fixed line is always a constant.
explain: A point that maintains a constant perpendicular distance from a fixed line traces a straight line parallel to it.

q: 32. The inclination of letters as recommended by BIS is .............
explain: As per Bureau of Indian Standards lettering conventions, sloping (italic) letters are recommended to be inclined at approximately 75° to the horizontal.

q: 33. When two graphic entities are at a constant distance apart along the length, commonly referred to as .............
explain: Two entities maintaining a constant distance apart along their length are, by geometric definition, described as parallel to each other — hence 'parallelism.'

q: 34. If a line intersects a circle at two points, not passing through the center, the line segment inside the circle is referred as .............
explain: A straight line segment connecting two points on a circle's circumference (not passing through the center, unlike a diameter) is called a chord.

q: 35. *The line connecting a view to note is called :
explain: A leader line is a thin, solid line used to connect a specific part of a drawing to a note, dimension, or symbol.

q: 36. CAD in engineering drawing represent for:
explain: CAD stands for Computer Aided Design.

q: 37. The view obtained after cutting the object in order to show the inner details by an imaginary cutting plane is known as
explain: This view, created by an imaginary cutting plane to reveal internal detail, is called a sectional view.

q: 38. Dimensions in a drawing are to be
explain: Once a drawing is dimensioned, values should be read directly from the figures given, not measured with a scale from the drawing itself.

q: 39. The regular polygon called nonagon has ............. members of equal sides.
explain: A nonagon, by definition, is a nine-sided polygon, so it has 9 equal sides in its regular form.

q: 40. The regular polygon called nonagon has ....... members of equal sides:
explain: A nonagon is a nine-sided regular polygon, with nine equal sides.

q: 41. Dimension lines and projection lines are drawn as
options: continuous thin line with zig zags
explain: Standard drafting practice dictates that dimension, extension, and projection lines should be continuous thin lines to distinguish them from object outlines.

q: 42. Generally written dimensions are followed and scaling out from the drawing is not allowed in
explain: Working drawings must be followed exactly as dimensioned; scaling measurements directly off the drawing is not permitted since reproduction can distort size.

q: 43. A line comprising of dots and small line segments in a site plan indicates
explain: A dot-dash line (dots and short dashes) is the conventional symbol used to indicate a property (boundary) line on site plans.

q: 44. Minimum distance between blackboard and first row of benches should not be less than ............. in school building.
explain: School design norms specify a minimum distance of 4 m between the blackboard and the first row of benches, ensuring students in front do not strain their eyes or necks.

q: 45. Engineering drawing indicates:
explain: An engineering drawing conveys the complete shape, size and dimensions of an object together.

q: 46. Minimum plinth level for school building is ............. above the road level.
explain: Building norms for school buildings require the plinth to be raised a minimum of 400 mm above the road level, protecting the structure from surface water and dampness.

q: 47. Dotted lines in drawing represent:
explain: Dotted (dashed) lines are the standard convention for showing hidden edges or surfaces not visible in the current view.

q: 48. If a point moves in a plane in such a way that the sum of its distances from two fixed points is constant the curve so traced is called .............
explain: This is the classical definition of an ellipse: the locus of points whose sum of distances from two fixed points (the foci) remains constant.

q: 49. Name the curve traced out by a point moving in a place such that the difference between its distances from two fixed points is constant .............
explain: By definition, a hyperbola is the locus of points where the difference (not sum) of distances from two fixed foci remains constant.

q: 50. Dimension lines and projection lines are shown as .............
options: continuous thin lines with zig zag
explain: As per standard line conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines.
